`SvelteSet`, `SvelteMap`, `SvelteURL`, `SvelteURLSearchParams`, `SvelteDate` and `MediaQuery` of `svelte/reactivity` are reactive already. Wrapping one in `$state()` adds nothing. The suggestion removes the `$state()`. The rule looks at components in runes mode and at `.svelte.js` and `.svelte.ts` files.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. It runs on the Svelte components that an ESLint config lints with `svelte-eslint-parser`, in the place of the rule of `eslint-plugin-svelte`:

{/* skip */}

```js eslint.config.js
import svelte from "eslint-plugin-svelte";

export default [
  ...svelte.configs.recommended,
  { rules: { "svelte/no-unnecessary-state-wrap": "error" } },
];
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}

```svelte
<script>
  import { SvelteSet } from "svelte/reactivity";

  const tags = $state(new SvelteSet());
</script>
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}

```svelte
<script>
  import { SvelteSet } from "svelte/reactivity";

  const tags = new SvelteSet();
</script>
```

## Options

| Option                      | Default | What it does                                                         |
| --------------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `additionalReactiveClasses` | `[]`    | More classes that are reactive already, by the name they are called  |
| `allowReassign`             | `false` | Allow the `$state()` around one where the variable is assigned again |
